title: Heat Pump Rebates in Niagara Falls 2026: Mild Winters, Wide Choice
desc: Niagara Falls heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings: 80% of households live in eligible house types, and a January low of -6.1C widens the choice of models.
h1: Heat Pump Rebates in Niagara Falls
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Niagara Falls has the mildest January in our Ontario data (-6.1°C). With 80% of its 37,795 households in eligible house types, many homeowners can apply.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Niagara Falls
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: The 2021 Census counts 13,845 owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981 in Niagara Falls. 66% of households live in detached houses and 70% own. 5.4% report needing major repairs. Only 4% live in tall apartments.

In a mild climate the program's lower sizing options make sense for gas and propane homes: option A (cooling emphasis) and option B (balanced) are open to them. Electric, oil and wood homes are limited to C and D. Niagara Falls owners on gas can therefore choose a system sized mainly for cooling.
Niagara Falls is served by Niagara Peninsula Energy (NPEI), not Alectra. NPEI does not set the heat pump rebate. The rate depends on the heating fuel you use now.
The program requires the home to be occupied for six months to avoid new builds and to have a primary heating system. Ask the program how it treats a home with part-year occupancy before you apply.

The contractor submits an itemized work order, photos of the existing heating system and nameplate, a signed participant agreement and the NRCan sizing form for each outdoor unit before the install. After the install the final invoice and photos follow within 30 days. A Niagara Falls owner should ask for copies of both filings.

A rented system pays $500 per ton up to $2,000 for any heating fuel, and a rented ground-source system pays $3,000 flat. Owned ground-source systems pay $2,000 per ton up to $12,000 for electric, oil, propane and wood homes and $3,000 flat for gas homes, if the loop is sized to the home's load.
claim_heading: How to claim in Niagara Falls
claim_steps: Choose a sizing option that matches how you want the heat pump to run.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
faq: Which sizing options can gas homes use?
Only after six months of occupancy.
